question: Revenue 1000cr, COGS 550cr, OpEx (excl D&A) 200cr, D&A 50cr, Interest 30cr, Other Income 10cr, Tax 45cr. EBITDA Margin?
before: EBITDA = 1000-550-200 = 250cr. Margin = 250/1000 = 25%. A (20%) subtracts D&A. C (45%) is Gross Margin. D subtracts interest and tax too.
after:
Formula: EBITDA Margin = EBITDA ÷ Revenue, where EBITDA = Revenue − COGS − Operating Expenses (excluding D&A). D&A, Interest, Tax, and Other Income are excluded from EBITDA calculation.

Step-by-step: First, calculate EBITDA by subtracting COGS and OpEx from Revenue: EBITDA = 1000 − 550 − 200 = 250 cr. Next, divide EBITDA by Revenue to get the margin: EBITDA Margin = 250 ÷ 1000 = 0.25 = 25%.

Result: EBITDA Margin is 25%.

Why this is correct: EBITDA margin measures operating profitability before financing and tax decisions. Option B correctly includes all revenue, subtracts only COGS and operating expenses (excluding depreciation and amortization), and expresses the result as a percentage of revenue.

Why the others are wrong: Option A (20%) incorrectly subtracts D&A from EBITDA, confusing EBITDA with EBIT. Option C (45%) calculates Gross Margin (Revenue minus COGS divided by Revenue), not operating margin. Option D (15%) appears to subtract Interest and Tax as well, fundamentally misunderstanding which line items belong in the EBITDA numerator.

Intuition: EBITDA margin isolates core operating profitability by removing the noise of capital structure (interest), tax policy, and accounting depreciation methods. For equity analysts, this metric reveals the true cash-generating power of a company's core business before financing decisions cloud the picture.
